newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian '97 crude output seen at 280 mln barrels.
newsitem.headline: Indian '97 crude output seen at 280 mln barrels.

text.p: Indian Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said on Thursday that 1997 crude oil production was projected to be about 280 million barrels.
Maran told a petroleum technology conference in the Indian capital that crude petroleum production fell by 10 percent in April-November 1996 compared with the same period in 1995.
"Annually, crude production is around 225 million barrels and is projected to be around 280 million barrels in 1997," Maran said in a written statement.
Maran said crude production grew by 19.3 percent in 1994/95 (April-March) and 7.2 percent in 1995/96.

"However, during the current fiscal year up to November 1996, there has been a sharp negative growth of 10 percent in the production figures which has been one of the primary factors for the current industrial slowdown," he said.
Maran said an expert committee had been set up. "I do hope that the crude petroleum sector will rise to the occasion to boost the production and help industrial pick-up," he said.
The industry minister said production of refinery products grew 6.3 percent in April-November 1996 against less than four percent growth rates in 1994/95 and 1995/96.
